title: Physicists once slowed light down to the speed of a car
body: In a vacuum, light covers about 300,000 km every second, but inside matter it can be dramatically slower. In 1998 a team led by Danish physicist Lene Hau sent a laser pulse through a cloud of sodium atoms chilled to a tiny fraction of a degree above absolute zero and slowed it to about 17 metres per second, roughly 60 km/h. A second laser made the cloud transparent but extremely sluggish. Her team later stopped light completely and then restarted it.
